Correspondence table between CIS-BP and TFClass

Source: R/data.R
tfclass_scheme.Rd

Table used by classify_tfs() to infer TFClass superclasses, classes, and families from CIS-BP families. The table was created by comparing the CIS-BP families of human TFs in CIS-BP (build 3.10) with their classifications in TFClass. CIS-BP families were assigned to the TFClass class of most of their TFs, and to the TFClass family of at least 90\ of their TFs (in this class) are listed, separated by ';' (e.g., CIS-BP's Homeodomain corresponds to TFClass families HOX, NK, and others). TFs in these CIS-BP families are assigned to a single TFClass family by classify_tfs() when possible (see classify_tfs() for details). Some entries were manually curated, including CIS-BP families with multiple types of DNA-binding domains (e.g., 'Homeodomain,POU') and CIS-BP's AT hook, whose TFClass family is the TFClass class 'A.T hook factors' (as CIS-BP's AT hook TFs include proteins other than those in HMGA, TFClass' only family in this class). CIS-BP families that are not in this table (e.g., families that do not occur in mammals, or with DNA-binding domains that are not classified by TFClass) are not classified by TFClass, except for families with multiple types of DNA-binding domains (see Details in ?classify_tfs).

Usage

data(tfclass_scheme)

Format

A data frame with the following variables:

CISBP_family

CIS-BP family.

TFClass_superclass

TFClass superclass.

TFClass_class

TFClass class.

TFClass_family

TFClass family, or all possible families separated by ';' if the CIS-BP family corresponds to more than one TFClass family. For CIS-BP families corresponding to a TFClass class but not to a specific family (i.e., AT hook), the TFClass class.

TFClass_ID

TFClass identifier(s) of the most specific classification level (class or family), separated by ';' if there are multiple families.

References

Wingender, E., Schoeps, T., Haubrock, M., Krull, M., & Dönitz, J. (2018). TFClass: expanding the classification of human transcription factors to their mammalian orthologs. Nucleic Acids Research, 46(D1), D343-D347.

Examples

data(tfclass_scheme)
